acknowledge_unwitnessed.reason: Polled by the bring-up before VOS is raised: the twin's PWR model reads it 1 always (AET-WO-4240v D-3), so no wait is witnessed; bench row B-2 reads PWR_CSR1 after boot.
Polled after VOS Scale 2 is written: the twin's PWR model reads it 1 always (AET-WO-4240v D-3), so no wait is witnessed; bench row B-2 reads PWR_D3CR after boot.
Depended on at reset and never written (AET-WO-4240v D-7): 7 WS and WRHIGHFREQ 11 judged against RM0433 Rev 9 Table 17 by the VOS rule; Renode models no flash wait state.
No model: the twin presents level 3 itself (4230 FEEDBACK section 2 m1). FAB-NOTES programs it by read-modify-write of OPTSR as read; the bench row reads bits 3:2 back as 11.
PA9/PA10 at AF7 for USART1: Renode's USART has no pin (4300b FEEDBACK section 0), so no AF choice shows in the twin. The bench row reads AFRH back after boot.
PA5-PA7 at AF5 for SPI1: the model routes a pin by AFR only for a timer channel (4300 FEEDBACK section 0). The bench row reads AFRL back; 3302 B2 predicted 0x555 there.
PA0 output (flash CS), PA5-PA7 and PA9/PA10 alternate: a BSRR write drives a pin whatever MODER says (4200 FEEDBACK). The bench row reads MODER back, as 3302 B2 did.
No edge rate is modelled; check speeds judges each chosen speed's fmax with svd-hal's own table, not an ir rule. The bench row reads OSPEEDR back.
OTYPER is not stored by Renode (4300b FEEDBACK section 10, measured): written whole, push-pull on every port A pin. The bench row reads it back, as 3302 B2 asked for GPIOB.
No pull is modelled. Written whole by split: no pull on the solved pins, the debug pins' reset pulls (PA13 up, PA14 down, PA15 up) kept. The bench row reads PUPDR back.
PB10/PB11 at AF4 for I2C2 (EXT): the model routes a pin by AFR only for a timer channel (4300 FEEDBACK section 0). The bench row reads AFRH back.
PB6/PB7 at AF4 for I2C1: the model routes a pin by AFR only for a timer channel (4300 FEEDBACK section 0). The bench row reads AFRL back; 3302 B2 predicted 0x44 there.
PB6/PB7 (I2C1) and PB10/PB11 (I2C2, EXT) alternate: the model routes a pin by MODER only for a timer channel (4300 FEEDBACK section 0). The bench row reads MODER back.
PB6/PB7 (I2C1, 400 kHz) and PB10/PB11 (I2C2, 100 kHz): no edge rate is modelled; check speeds judges fmax with svd-hal's own table, not an ir rule. The bench row reads OSPEEDR back.
OTYPER is not stored by Renode (4300b FEEDBACK section 10): PB6/PB7 (I2C1) and PB10/PB11 (I2C2) open-drain, the rest push-pull. The bench row reads it back on silicon.
No pull is modelled. Written whole by split: no internal pull on PB6/PB7 (2.2 kOhm) or PB10/PB11 (10 kOhm), PB4's reset pull-up kept. The bench row reads PUPDR back.
PE is set by the enable, not by silicon::i2c_cr1 (whose word has PE clear); stored, with no reaction claimed. The bench row reads PE as 1; the bus records on the bench need it.
7-bit addressing, no reload, no PEC, written 0 (AUTOEND set at run time): STM32F7_I2C.cs is not held, no reaction claimed. The bench row reads CR2 back, all but AUTOEND.
Write-1-to-clear (RM0433 Rev 9 section 47.9.8, p. 2015), so no bench row: STOPCF and NACKCF after each transfer. The next record's OK status on the bench (3302 B3) shows the clear took.
PE is set by the enable, not by silicon::i2c_cr1 (whose word has PE clear); stored, with no reaction claimed. The bench row reads PE as 1 on the EXT bus.
7-bit addressing, no reload, no PEC, written 0: the firmware starts no transfer on EXT (no device), so AUTOEND stays 0; no reaction claimed. The bench row reads CR2 back as 0.
Write-1-to-clear (RM0433 Rev 9 section 47.9.8, p. 2015), written only by a transfer, and the firmware makes none on EXT (no device). No bench row: write-only.
I2C2's clock enable for the EXT bus (no device on it): stored, with no reaction claimed and no I2C2 device modelled. The bench row reads APB1LENR back.
Not polled (ruling on Q-F): STM32H7_RCC.cs L175 keeps it a tag reading 0, so a wait would park every boot. Silicon must read 1 after a D2 enable: a bench row (3302).
A tag in Renode (STM32H7_RCC.cs L401, read 0 whatever is written, 4230 FEEDBACK section 2). SPI1's kernel per_ck assumes HSI here; the bench row reads it, as 3302 B8.
ResetClock reads them at reset before the select write; a tag (STM32H7_RCC.cs L408-410) reads 0 whatever silicon holds. The written SPI123SEL is judged by spi_words.
Left at reset (rcc_pclk2/pclk1 kernels the BRR and TIMINGR rules assume); a tag (STM32H7_RCC.cs L420-425) reads 0 whatever silicon holds. The bench row reads each.
The FPU enable in the generated Reset, outside every Kani harness; whether Renode faults a float with CPACR clear is not held. The bench row reads CP10/CP11 as full access.
A tag (STM32H7_SPI.cs L149), written 0 with TSIZE: no reload is used. The bench row reads it back as 0.
Tags in Renode (STM32H7_SPI.cs L258-266), written 0 beside EOTC; write-only, so no bench row. The boot record's flash identity, read on silicon, shows each transfer ended.
MODF is a tag (STM32H7_SPI.cs L238) and MASTER always reads 1: no mode fault in the twin. SSM|SSI before SPE is proved by Kani; the bench row reads MODF as 0 (3302 saw it 1).
Not stored by Renode's USART (4300b FEEDBACK section 0; M0, M1 measured P4.1): 8 data bits, FIFO off, no wake-up, interrupts off. The bench row reads CR1 back.
Stored with no reaction claimed (4300b FEEDBACK section 0): no parity, oversampling by 16, interrupts off, compared with the topology only. The bench row reads CR1 back.
STOP is the only CR2 field Renode stores (4300b FEEDBACK section 0; RXINV, TXINV measured P4.1): asynchronous, no swap, no inversion, LSB first. The bench row reads CR2 back.
One stop bit: stored, no reaction claimed (4300b FEEDBACK section 0), compared with the topology only. The bench row reads CR2.STOP back as 00.

accept_lifecycle.statement: The board's SPI flash, NRND by its maker (Winbond's catalog, Status-Industrial N, 2026-11-16) with longevity support listed; kept until AET-WO-4500 picks a flash in mass production (AET-WO-4211)
